region.text: Reuss-Lobenstein, passed to the Ebersdorf line

ledger.note: 1824: the Lobenstein line dies out and its land passes to Ebersdorf. 'Schon 1824 erlosch aber durch den Tod von Heinrich LIV. die Linie Reuß-Lobenstein'; the Principality page: 'The territories of four separate branches of the Junior Line amalgamated between 1824 and 1848'. A union inside the Junior Line, which Cliopatria draws as one state throughout; no outline changes.

1848: the Junior Line is united under Reuss-Schleiz. 'Diese Linie verzichtete 1848 mit der Abdankung des Fürsten Heinrich LXXII. zugunsten der Linie Reuß-Schleiz'; infobox 'Union of line of Junior Reuss: 1848'. Another union inside the Junior Line; no outline changes.
1848: the state is officially the Principality of Reuss Junior Line ('officially called the Principality of Reuss Junior Line' after 1848), later Fürstentum Reuß jüngerer Linie.

ledger.note: 11 November 1918: the principality is disestablished (infobox 'Disestablished: 11 November 1918'). 'When the German Empire collapsed at the end of World War I, the reigning Prince Reuss lost his crown along with all the other monarchs whose realms were within Germany'; 'the territory of the Junior Line merged with that of the Elder Line in 1919 as the People's State of Reuss'. The page gives no 1871-1918 dates for the Empire; the 'States of the German Empire' page lists 'Reuss-Gera (Junior line)' as a principality of the Empire. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

certainty.note: A small state with administrative boundaries; the pages name towns and exclaves (Triebes, Hohenleuben, Pohlen) but no survey, and the grid outline cannot draw them. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes:
ONE STATE OR FOUR? Cliopatria's single row follows the Wikipedia article 'Principality of Reuss-Gera', which is the Reuss Junior Line (Fürstentum Reuß jüngerer Linie): until 1848 it was several sovereign principalities (Schleiz with Gera, Lobenstein, Ebersdorf), joined by the 1824 and 1848 events. This dossier keeps them as one state, as the Cliopatria shape does.

THE ELDER LINE. Cliopatria's shape (1,987 to 2,186 km2) also holds Greiz, the capital of the separate Principality of Reuss Elder Line (Reuss-Greiz, 'united' in 1778 and extinct in 1927, House of Reuss page); no Cliopatria row exists for it. COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Principality of Reuss-Greiz (Reuss Elder Line), suggested slug principality-of-reuss-greiz, 1778-1918 (group eu-20-x); when it exists, subtract its land from this dossier's shapes.

SHAPES. The 1815-1819 shape (3,180 km2) is wrong (other states' lands; no page records a gain). The Gera cell is missing from every shape and is added. The grid (about 250 km2 a cell) overstates a state of 827 km2.

END YEAR 1871 follows the sibling German-state dossiers; the monarchy lasted to 11 November 1918.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The accession to the Confederation of the Rhine (April 1807; the Confederation page dates the Reuss principalities to 11 and 18 April 1807) and to the German Confederation (1815) are association memberships and not ledger events; neither Reuss page gives the 1807 date. (2) The Principality page's infobox says 'Established: 1802' and 'Raised to principality: 9 April 1806'. (3) The infobox ruler list is the Schleiz line; the Lobenstein and Ebersdorf princes before 1848 are not listed. (4) Reuss-Köstritz (a non-governing branch; prince in 1806 'without governmental power') is not a state.

GAZETTEER: Gera is in places.jsonl; Schleiz, Lobenstein and Ebersdorf are not named in the regions. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (principality-of-reuss-gera_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row principality-of-reuss-gera -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. The Reuss-Gera page does not date the Empire membership; the States of the German Empire page lists it. The People's State of Reuss (1919, with the Elder Line) has no dossier.
